name: Offline Neural Text to Speech
tagline: A natural-sounding voice for every app on your computer — offline, no key, no cloud.
description:
Offline Neural Text to Speech is a PROVIDER app: install it, keep it in your Providers folder, and assign it to the Text → speech AI type in Settings → AI models. From then on, every app that asks GifOS to speak — Reader, games, anything using the ai ability — is answered by this app, entirely on your device.

The voice is KittenTTS Nano (Apache-2.0), a 15-million-parameter neural model with eight voices: Bella, Jasper, Luna, Bruno, Rosie, Hugo, Kiki and Leo. It also answers to the familiar names apps already use (nova, shimmer, fable, echo, onyx, alloy), so anything written for a cloud voice works unchanged.

THE TRADE, PLAINLY. This is a much better voice than the other offline option — and a heavier one. The engine rides inside the GIF, but the 24 MB voice model is downloaded once, checked against a SHA-256 fixed in the app, and kept on your computer. It also takes noticeably longer to start talking than the robotic voice does, and how much longer depends on your device — a laptop and an old phone are not the same machine.

So this does not replace Offline Text to Speech. Keep both: the little one is 1.6 MB, instant, and never downloads anything; this one sounds like a person. Switch between them any time in Settings → AI models.

Once the voice is on your device it never asks the network again. The app itself cannot: a Provider app is refused any network capability at all, so nothing you ask it to say can leave this browser.
author: GifOS
